In-store furniture commerce platform

European home-furnishing retailer · Technical ArchitectJun 2025 – Present

An iPad progressive web app used by sales staff in the showroom to configure custom furniture with customers and sell it directly. It replaced a 1990s DOS-based configuration system and is live in 3 stores.

TeamTeam of 8: technical architect (me), delivery manager, front-end lead, front-end developer, 3 full-stack developers, tester.
StackJava 21, Spring Boot, Angular PWA, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Redis, BigQuery, Google Pub/Sub, Cloud Run, GitLab CI, Cloud Logging & Monitoring

What I did

  • Architected a data-driven platform on Java 21, Spring Boot, Angular PWA and GCP Cloud Run, from first requirement in Jun 2025 to production in Nov 2025, as a modular monolith (PIM + Sales: ordering, discounts, delivery, payments, contracts) built to split into microservices for a future warehouse and ERP phase.
  • Designed the data-driven product configurator and rule builder (guided flows and 2D drag-and-drop) that keeps every configuration consistent; 50+ suppliers onboarded, each with its own rule set, without code changes.
  • Introduced event-driven integration with Google Pub/Sub across modules, stock monitoring, BigQuery analytics and an AI service that converts supplier brochures into structured product data.
  • Cut product configuration time from ~60 min to 5–8 min; 100+ orders/day across 3 stores and growing; search under 500 ms with Elasticsearch.
  • Technical architect for a team of 8; 3-week sprints with weekly or biweekly rapid releases via GitLab CI; works directly with the client, including on-site visits to the Netherlands.

Key architecture decisions

Modular monolith over microservicesA data-driven platform had to reach production in about six months with a small team. Clear module boundaries (PIM, Sales) keep a later split into microservices open for the planned warehouse and ERP phase.
Data-driven configurator and rule builderProducts, options and validity rules live in data, not code, so new suppliers and product ranges go live without a release. Supports both guided flows and a 2D drag-and-drop builder.
Events with Google Pub/SubStock updates, analytics feeds and supplier imports are decoupled from the sales flow, so a slow consumer never blocks a sale in the store.
